Static HTML project is ideal: index.html at root, no package.json. Also AGENTS.md mentions port 3002 for Pascal dev server but default is 3000; irrelevant.

Now build the game. Scope: a polished top-down GTA-style game in canvas 2D with:

- Procedural city grid (blocks, roads, buildings, parks, water?)
- Player on foot with WASD/arrows, enter/exit cars (E)
- Multiple cars parked and traffic
- Driving physics (accel/brake/steer, drift feel), collisions with buildings/cars
- Pedestrians wandering, can be hit (keep it non-graphic, they ragdoll/flee)
- Police wanted system with star levels, cop cars chase
- Missions: steal specific car and deliver to marker, or collect packages; earn cash
- HUD: health, cash, wanted stars, minimap, mission text
- Mobile: virtual joystick + action buttons, touch-friendly, responsive
- Sound optional via WebAudio simple engine hum and effects (needs user gesture)
- Pause/menu, save best score in localStorage

That's a lot. Keep code organized in files: index.html, styles.css, js modules (game.js, city.js, entities.js, input.js, hud.js, audio.js). Since static server supports modules fine.

I should be careful about time/tokens. Aim for ~1500-2000 lines total, well-structured, then test with playwright screenshot per Agents.md, iterating until visuals good.

Name: "Sunset City: Grand Auto" or "GTA-style" — avoid trademark. I'll title it "VICE RUN — Grand Theft Auto-style sandbox" but that's marketing. Call it "Sunset City" with subtitle "a GTA-inspired open-world toy". Original assets, no copied content.

Let me design mechanics concretely:

World: 4096x4096 city grid, cell size 512; roads width 96 around blocks. Buildings occupy inner block areas with margins, random heights/colors, drawn with fake shadows and rooftops. Parks replace some blocks (grass + trees). Water on edges? Keep land.

Camera follows player, zoom based on speed.

Entities:
- Player: on foot (walk, sprint), or in car.
- Cars: AI traffic following road lanes on grid; police AI; parked cars.
- Peds: wander sidewalks; flee when gunshots or nearby crash; can be hit -> "down" (non-graphic, just lie down and disappear); increases wanted.
- Police: spawn based on wanted, chase player, ram; if player on foot nearby, they shoot (damage). Wanted decays when out of sight/timer.

Weapons: punch? Keep a pistol with limited ammo? Simpler: player has a pistol with infinite ammo but shooting increases wanted; bullets. Or skip shooting to keep scope? GTA without shooting on foot is fine but less fun. Include simple shooting (click or button) with bullets hitting peds/cops/cars.

Missions: "Sunset Delivery" — markers: go to a car (marked), steal it, drive to dropoff within time; payout. Continual mission loop with randomized pickups. Also collecting cash pickups scattered.

HUD: top-left health bar, cash, top-right wanted stars, minimap bottom-right (canvas), mission banner top-center, speedometer bottom-left when driving.

Mobile: left joystick, right buttons: enter/exit (E), shoot (F), sprint/brake? For driving, joystick steers and accelerate? Simplest mobile driving: same joystick controls direction of car relative (up = accelerate, left/right steer, down = brake); action button = handbrake. On foot joystick moves, shoot button fires in facing direction, enter button.

Keyboard: WASD/arrows, Shift sprint/handbrake, E enter/exit, F/Space shoot, Esc pause.

Traffic AI: cars move along road center lanes on a grid, turning at intersections randomly; simple: each car has a target waypoint at next intersection center with lane offset; drive straight toward it, then pick next direction. Collisions with player car push them.

To keep performance: ~24 traffic cars, ~40 peds, cull rendering by viewport.

Roads: define grid: blocks of 512 with 96 road width on each boundary. Roads at x = k*512 (centered), width 96. Lane offset 24 each side. Buildings drawn inside block interior area: block interior from k*512+48+? Let's structure:

CELL = 512. Road center lines at multiples of CELL. Road half width 48. Block area between road edges: from k*CELL+48 to (k+1)*CELL-48 => 416x416. Inside, buildings grid of 2x2 or random footprint with sidewalk margin 16. Sidewalk: draw light gray band from road edge to +16.

Collision: buildings are AABBs. Also world bounds.

Driving physics: car has pos, angle, vel (speed scalar along angle + lateral drift). Simple arcade: speed += throttle*accel*dt - drag; angle += steer * speed factor * dt. Add slight drift visual via velocity vector lerp. Collide with buildings: push out and reduce speed.

Car vs car collision: circle-ish AABB? Use rotated rectangle vs rotated rectangle is complex; use two-circle approximation per car (front/rear circles radius ~14). Resolve push apart and transfer speed.

Ped collision/culling.

Rendering style: retro-ish vibrant: dark asphalt with dashed lines, sidewalks, buildings with colored facades, rooftops with AC units, trees circles, car sprites drawn as rounded rect with windshield, roof, lights. Nice shadows. Night/day? Do dusk palette (sunset) fixed — "Sunset City". Add subtle vignette and scanline? Keep clean.

Minimap: draw roads grid scaled, player arrow, mission marker, cops.

Wanted system: 0-5 stars. Crimes: hitting ped (+1), shooting (+1 per shot up to), ramming cop car (+1). Cop spawn rate. When wanted>0, cops chase; if busted (cops close while on foot) or health 0 => "WASTED"/"BUSTED" screen with respawn at hospital/police, lose cash.

Pause overlay & start screen with controls and "Start" button (needed for audio gesture).

Audio: WebAudio engine oscillator for engine when driving, pitch by speed; siren for cops (two-tone), gunshot noise, crash. Keep modest with mute toggle.

That's substantial but doable. Let me write files.

File plan:
- index.html: canvas + HUD DOM overlays (start screen, pause, wasted, touch controls, mission text, stats).
- styles.css
- js/main.js: bootstrap, loop, resize.
- js/world.js: city gen, collision, rendering world (roads/buildings/parks), minimap data.
- js/entities.js: Car, Ped, Bullet, Player classes? Might be one big file for simplicity with clear sections.
- js/game.js: game state, updates, missions, wanted, HUD updates, input wiring.
- js/input.js: keyboard/touch joystick.
- js/audio.js.

To reduce inter-module friction, maybe 4 files: input.js, audio.js, world.js, game.js, main.js.

Design details:

World constants:
CELL=560, ROAD=110 (half 55), GRID=8 => world 8*560=4480.
Road centers at x=i*CELL for i=0..GRID.
Blocks between roads: for i in 0..GRID-1, block rect x0=i*CELL+55, x1=(i+1)*CELL-55 (450 wide incl sidewalks). Sidewalk width 22 inside block; building zone x0+22.

Actually sidewalk should be outside building zone but part of block. Roads at boundaries. Draw sidewalk as block background light color (whole block), then buildings inset.

Block types: park (10%), parking lot (10%), buildings (80%). Buildings: 1-4 per block with gaps; each has color palette, height visual offset (draw top face offset opposite? top-down with 2.5D: draw building footprint offset by height*0.06 toward camera? Simpler: draw shadow offset down-right, then facade rect, then roof inset with lighter shade, plus AC boxes). Height affects roof offset: draw facade at footprint, roof drawn inset by h*0.03 offset up-left, giving pseudo-3D.

Collision uses footprint only.

Buildings visible in map? Minimap just roads + blocks shading maybe skip.

Roads: draw asphalt as full world background dark? Alternative: draw all roads by filling world asphalt, then draw blocks (sidewalk+grass) on top, then lane markings. That's efficient: background = asphalt; for each block draw sidewalk rect + interior. Lane markings along each road center? Roads between blocks; center dashed lines along each road at i*CELL from 0..world. Draw dashes.

Crosswalks at intersections: white stripes. Nice detail.

Traffic AI route: waypoint nodes at intersections with lane offsets. Simpler approach: car follows a road axis; at intersection center decides to continue or turn. Implement: each AI car has dir (0..3), lane offset, target = next intersection along dir with offset applied. When within ~12 of target, choose new dir (not reverse unless dead end), set target next intersection. Compute target point = intersection + perpendicular lane offset. Need consistent right-hand traffic: if moving +x, lane offset y=+LANE (right side); moving -x, y=-LANE; moving +y, x=-LANE; +? Let's define: dir vector d, right vector r = (-d.y, d.x). Offset = r * lane (24). Target point = intersectionCenter + r*lane? Approaching intersection, the car should be in its lane before intersection. When turning, target next node includes offset. Cars will cut corners slightly, fine.

AI speed ~ 90-140 px/s. Avoid player? Basic: if obstacle ahead (player car/ped/car) within 60, slow/stop. Keep simple: cars brake if another car within 55 ahead in same direction.

Cops: spawn on road outside view, chase player directly (ignore roads) with speed based on wanted; shoot when close and player on foot? Cops on foot? Keep cop cars only, plus cops exit car when player on foot & near? That's complex. Cop cars ram and damage player; when player on foot and cop car within 60, player takes damage over time ("busted" meter?). Simpler: cop cars shoot bullets at player when within 400 and line of sight ignoring buildings? Bullets damage. Cops also ram.

Wanted decay: if no crime for 12s and no cop within 500, lose 1 star each 8s.

Health regen slight after 8s no damage.

- Type A "Hot Wheels": steal marked car (glowing marker at a random parked car), drive it to drop marker. Reward $500-1200.
- Type B "Package run": collect 3 packages (markers) on foot/in car within timer. Reward.
- Type C "Taxi": pick up passenger marker, drive to destination, keep car intact? Simpler skip.
Let's do type A and B alternating; also random cash pickups ($50) around city.

Mission flow: start at drop marker? Keep one active objective at a time with arrow pointer to target and distance. "Deliver the car" requires being in target car and stopping in marker zone for 2s? Just enter zone -> complete.

## Objective
- User sent only "Gta 5" with no further instruction; since the non-interactive run could not ask a clarifying question, the assistant assumed they wanted a GTA 5–style browser game built in this empty OMGithub PlayGround repo.
- Build an original, playable open-world driving/crime sandbox ("Sunset City") with no copied assets.

## Requirements
- Original code/art only; explicitly unofficial and not affiliated with Rockstar Games (disclaimer included in UI).
- Static HTML project served on port 3002; must run in browser, responsive and mobile-friendly with touch controls.
- No user requirements beyond "Gta 5" (ambiguity unresolved).

## Decisions
- Built "Sunset City": top-down procedural city, on-foot + driving, carjacking, traffic, peds, police wanted stars, missions (repo/courier), cash pickups, minimap, synthesized audio, touch joystick/buttons.
- Split large code into modules to stay within output limits.
- Fixed a bug where AI traffic hitting peds raised the player's wanted level; crime now only attributed via `byPlayer` flag.
- Improved flat visuals: 2.5D building facades, more building layouts, rooftop detail, sidewalk tiles, street trees, lamps, manholes, warm palette.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html`, `styles.css`, and all JS modules written and syntax-checked (`node --check` on copies in `/tmp/opencode/check/`).
- Local server running in tmux session `sunset` (`PORT=3002 ./start.sh`); page returns 200.

### Active
- Performance investigation: measured ~7 FPS at 1280x800 with rendering on, 60 FPS with `render` no-op.
- Per-section Java timings (not yet conclusive; totals only ~1.5 ms): ground 0.5, entities 0.9, HUD FX 0.1, minimap 0 ms — suggests browser/SwiftShader flush costs rather than JS logic.

1. Profile/optimize rendering for software-rendered Chromium; likely canvas cache of static city ground (block/2x2-cell tiles or scaled world layer), reduce per-frame paths/strokes/radial gradients, and consider `ctx` alpha:false / lower pixel ratio.

# Sunset City

An original, fan-made open-world crime sandbox that runs entirely in the browser. No commercial game assets are used: the city, cars, characters, interface, and synthesized audio are generated by this project's own code.

> Unofficial tribute. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Rockstar Games.

## Play

The project is a static site with ES modules, so serve it over HTTP rather than opening `index.html` directly.

```bash
python3 -m http.server 3002
```

Then open <http://localhost:3002>.

## Controls

| Input | On foot | In a vehicle |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `WASD` / arrow keys | Move | Drive / steer |
| `Shift` | Sprint | Handbrake |
| `E` | Enter a nearby vehicle | Exit (when slow) |
| `F` / click | Shoot | — |
| `Esc` / `P` | Pause / resume | Pause / resume |
| `M` | Mute | Mute |

On phones and tablets, a virtual joystick, `ENTER`, `FIRE`, and `BRAKE` buttons appear automatically.

## Features

- Procedurally generated city with parks, parking lots, rooftop details, street furniture, and traffic.
- On-foot exploration, carjacking, driving physics, collisions, and chases.
- Pedestrians, police response, a five-star wanted system, and wanted-level cooldown.
- Repeatable courier and vehicle-repo jobs, cash pickups, health, damage, and respawning.
- Minimap, objective markers and direction arrow, synthesized engine/siren/SFX audio.
- Responsive HUD and touch controls, plus a cached static city layer for smoother rendering.

## Source layout

- `index.html`, `styles.css` — shell, HUD, menus, overlays, and responsive styling.
- `js/game.js` — game state, input actions, player/camera, driving.
- `js/world.js` — city generation, collision, static city rendering.
- `js/systems.js` — traffic, pedestrians, police, missions, pickups, particles.
- `js/render.js` — world/entity rendering, markers, cached ground layer, screen feedback.
- `js/hud.js` — DOM HUD and minimap.
- `js/input.js` — keyboard, mouse, and touch input.
- `js/audio.js` — synthesized Web Audio engine, siren, and effects.
- `js/main.js` — bootstrap and animation loop.

## Serve with the provided runner

If the workspace runtime provides one, `./start.sh` starts the project on the configured port.
